summary:
Hello everyone!
We are the R2-SteadSound team, and today we are proud to introduce our web-based astronomical jukebox—a project born from a mission to bridge the gap between space exploration and sensory accessibility for the blind and visually impaired community. 
Our platform takes breathtaking official NASA imagery from the Hubble and Roman space telescopes and translates them into rich, immersive soundscapes. Using a custom pixel-recognition engine that analyzes tone, hue, and light values, the web app sonifies the cosmos in real-time.
Built with a Python backend and a responsive HTML/CSS frontend, the audio experience is powered by JavaScript and the library Tone.js. Best of all, users have full creative control over their cosmic listening experience: you can customize the instrumentation to suit your taste—from grand classical orchestras to modern rock arrangements, or even blended crossover genres. The cosmos is yours to tune!
details:
What does it do?

SteadSound transforms images of space into sound, allowing users to explore the universe through listening.

Users can select astronomical images, explore them pixel by pixel using their mouse or keyboard, and hear each pixel translated into sound based on its color, brightness and vibrance. They can choose and combine different instruments, or play the entire image as a short musical composition.With audio guidance and keyboard navigation, people who are blind or have low vision can independently explore the platform. SteadSound turns the visual beauty of space into an accessible auditory experience.

how is our proyect creative? SteadSound's creativity lies in combining space exploration with accessibility through a unique sensory experience. Rather than simply displaying images of space, our project allows users to discover them through sound, using mathematics to convert the information from each RGB pixel into sound waves that users can experience simulating an orchestra that can be experience

What factors did we consider?

Accessibility was our main priority. We considered that navigating a website can be challenging for people who are blind or have low vision. To address this, we implemented audio navigation and auditory guidance to make the experience more intuitive and accessible.

Our goal was to ensure that users could independently navigate through the different sections of our platform, explore the image jukebox, select their preferred sounds and enjoy the experience without relying entirely on visual elements.

We also considered the importance of making the sonification meaningful and understandable, so that sound would not only guide users through the interface but also allow them to explore and interpret images of space.
